source.title: Evaluating the Impact of Model Scale for Compositional Generalization in Semantic Parsing
source.authors: Linlu Qiu; Peter Shaw; Panupong Pasupat; Tian-Ze Shi; Jonathan Herzig; E. Pitler; F. Sha; K. Toutanova

record.tranche_reason: The study measures downstream exact-match performance across model sizes, testing scale-related downstream performance trends with a different measure from pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates exact-match accuracy on semantic parsing tasks, not held-out language-model cross-entropy, pretraining loss extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocations. Rows record selected accuracy scaling curves relevant to V6. The text also reports trends in syntax errors, recombination errors, output length, and trigram-LM agreement; these are not exact-match performance measures named by V6 and are not separately rowed here. Cited scaling-law findings from other papers are not study results.
record.test_reason: The study measures downstream exact-match accuracy on compositional semantic parsing across T5 (60M–11B) and PaLM (8B–540B) under three adaptation methods. Its headline result is that fine-tuning gives flat or negative scaling curves, which directly qualifies V6's claim that downstream performance improves predictably with scale. It is a new setting with results that argue V6 needs restating, rather than a same-method replication, so T5 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The authors also state that the flat fine-tuning curves are not likely due to performance saturation. They add that better retrievers, alternative output formats and constrained decoding might let scale be leveraged better.
record.recipe_differences: Measures semantic-parsing exact-match accuracy across pretrained model sizes and task-adaptation methods, rather than pretraining cross-entropy, power-law fits, or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling trend changes with task-adaptation method and dataset/split. In-context learning performance is also described as highly dependent on the retriever. The study notes that tuning hyperparameters separately at each model scale could change results, but does not do so.

fits_no_version.finding: Error-type trends with scale: unbalanced-parenthesis syntax errors generally fall with size, but fine-tuned larger T5 models more often copy training outputs or single-domain programs and agree more with a trigram LM over training outputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling changes the composition of downstream errors (better output syntax, more overfitting to the training output distribution under fine-tuning).

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), 2022
record.problems: The authors did not perform multiple runs for each split because of computation costs. They aggregate results by dataset to reduce variance; accuracy uncertainty estimates are not reported. Evaluation uses subsets of COGS and CFQ, and the reported accuracy curves concern semantic parsing rather than pretraining loss.
record.rows_left_out: Additional per-split and per-model accuracy results in Tables 6-7 and scaling plots in Figures 2, 7-11 are omitted to stay within the row limit; the selected rows retain representative positive, flat, negative, and non-monotonic trends across adaptation methods and task settings.

untested.parts: Prediction of downstream performance from pretraining loss. No fitted functional form or extrapolation of downstream accuracy; 'predictably' is not assessed beyond direction of change.
Extrapolation of loss from small runs.
Power-law form in other modalities or regimes. Fine-tuning is studied, but only as downstream accuracy with no power-law fit.

missing.what: Aggregated scaling curves per dataset over all compositional splits. These are the basis of the authors' headline claim that fine-tuning is flat/negative except on CFQ.
Further fine-tuning results that are flat or reversed, e.g. T5 FT on SMCalFlow-CS 8-C (15.8, 21.7, 6.9, 9.2, 11.4) and COGS Gen. (88.7→89.8).
In-distribution splits show flat fine-tuning curves, partly from saturation at 100%. On a 1K-example down-sampled CFQ in-distribution split, the T5 fine-tuning curve is still negative.
Output-format comparison: scaling trends similar across original and intermediate representations.

record.verdict_notes: All values checked against Tables 6–7 and match. The results are single runs with no uncertainty, so small differences (<2 points) are treated as flat. Hyperparameters were tuned only on smaller models (T5-base/PaLM-8B for FT, T5-3B for PT), a possible confound for the large-model fine-tuning results that the authors acknowledge. The axis is model size only, with no compute or token variation and no fitted law, so V6's 'predictably' is unassessed beyond direction of change. The T5 and PaLM families differ in architecture and pretraining, so cross-family comparisons are not scaling evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs' pretraining loss from small-run fits.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Power-law scaling in other modalities or training regimes.

The study tests downstream exact-match accuracy against model scale on semantic parsing datasets and adaptation methods. It does not test prediction from pretraining loss or fit a general predictive law.
Fitted exponents, compute-optimal split, parameter-counting or fitting choices, and departures of pretraining-loss curves from power laws.

relationships.condition: In-context learning with PaLM 8B→540B (non-oracle retriever) on COGS Gen., GeoQuery Length and Template1; prompt-tuned T5 on CFQ MCD1; fine-tuned PaLM 8B→62B on CFQ MCD3
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises steadily with size: ICL 32.1→58.8, 28.8→57.9, 25.9→74.1; PT 0.0→66.9; PaLM FT 19.1→41.4 (r16-r22, r28-r36).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy increased 32.1→58.8 on COGS, 28.8→57.9 on GeoQuery Length and 25.9→74.1 on Template1 with in-context learning, 0.0→66.9 with T5 prompt tuning, and 19.1→41.4 with PaLM fine-tuning.

relationships.condition: Full fine-tuning of T5 60M→11B on GeoQuery Length and Template1 compositional splits
relationships.reason: No gain from a 180x size increase: 40.3→38.5 on Length and 85.8→86.1 on Template1, with dips at Large/3B. Authors call fine-tuning curves flat or negative (r1-r5, r11-r15).
relationships.display_finding: A 180-fold size increase changed Length accuracy from 40.3 to 38.5 and Template1 accuracy from 85.8 to 86.1, with intermediate dips at Large and 3B.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: Full fine-tuning of T5 60M→11B on GeoQuery Length and Template1 compositional splits
source_check.reason: Table 6 shows Length declining from 40.3 to 38.5 and Template1 remaining nearly unchanged from 85.8 to 86.1, with intermediate dips; the authors explicitly describe flat or negative fine-tuning curves.

relationships.condition: Fine-tuned T5 on CFQ MCD3; prompt-tuned T5 on GeoQuery Length; PaLM ICL on SMCalFlow-CS 8-C
relationships.reason: Gains are non-monotonic or confined to part of the range: FT peaks at 3B (35.1) then drops to 29.8 at 11B; PT is flat until 3B; ICL stays near zero up to 540B (4.7) (r6-r10, r23-r27, r37-r39).
relationships.display_finding: Fine-tuned T5 peaks at 35.1 at 3B before falling to 29.8 at 11B, prompt-tuned T5 stays flat until 3B, and PaLM in-context performance remains near zero at 4.7 even at 540B.
